title: Performance
summary: Finding jank on the JS and UI threads, avoiding wasted renders with memo and stable props, list tuning, startup time and profiling.

sections.title: Measure first
sections.body: Turn on the performance monitor to see JS and UI frame rates. A drop in JS FPS means your React code or logic is busy; a drop in UI FPS means native rendering or layout is heavy. Profile in a release build: development builds run extra checks and are much slower. Use the React profiler to see which components render and why.

sections.title: Wasted renders
sections.body: Each render of a list row costs JS time. `React.memo` skips a render when props are shallowly equal, but only if the props really are equal: a new inline object, array or arrow function on every parent render defeats it. Keep callbacks stable with `useCallback`, derived data stable with `useMemo`, and pass primitives where you can. With the React Compiler enabled, much of this memoisation is automatic.

sections.title: Lists, images and startup
sections.body:
- Give `FlatList` a stable `renderItem`, `keyExtractor` and `getItemLayout` when heights are fixed.
- Keep rows light; avoid heavy work in `renderItem`.
- Resize images to their display size and cache them.
- Use Hermes, lazy-load screens and defer non-critical work until after the first frame (`InteractionManager.runAfterInteractions` or a timeout).
- Remove `console.log` in release builds: logging crosses to native code and is slow.

sections.title: Practising it here
sections.body: Exercises here run as TypeScript in a browser sandbox with no React Native runtime, so they model this logic as plain functions and reducers. The same functions drop straight into a real app: call them from a component, a hook or a store. The exercise implements the shallow comparison `React.memo` uses and a memoised selector.

pitfalls: Wrapping everything in `memo` while still passing new inline objects as props.
Doing heavy synchronous work in a press handler before giving feedback.

gotchas.question: A memoised row still re-renders every time. The parent passes `style={{ margin: 4 }}`. Why?
gotchas.answer: The inline object is new on every render, so the shallow comparison sees a changed prop. Hoist it into `StyleSheet.create` or a constant.

gotchas.question: JS FPS is 60 but UI FPS drops during a scroll. Where do you look?
gotchas.answer: Native rendering: overdraw, large images, complex shadows or too many views. The JS thread is not the bottleneck.

gotchas.question: Is `shallowEqual({ a: [1] }, { a: [1] })` true?
gotchas.answer: No. The arrays are different objects, so the values compare unequal by reference, even with the same contents.
